newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus to register 3.5 pct GDP growth in 97-govt.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus to register 3.5 pct GDP growth in 97-govt.

text.p: Cyprus's economy is expected to register a growth of up to 3.5 percent in its gross domestic product in 1997, up from an estimated 1.9 percent growth rate in 1996, government economists have said in a report.

Official forecasts are based on the assumption that the external environment will be more favourable than 1996, and that a negative climate among investors which prevailed in Cyprus last year will subside, the government-run Planning Bureau said in its annual report obtained by Reuters on Friday.
Issuing an assessment of economic trends of 1996, and forecasts for 1997, the Planning Bureau said the main characteristic of last year was an economic slowdown, due mainly to external factors.

"The Cyprus economy was negatively affected by restrained economic growth in the European Union, further liberalisation of world trade, and the rise in oil prices in the international markets, which implies the transfer of resources from oil-importing countries, such as Cyprus, to oil-producing countries," it said.

But the report also highlighted a restrained outbreak of meningitis last year, violence along the United Nations controlled buffer zone splitting the island and an earthquake in October as factors which affected the general climate of confidence among investors and consumers in Cyprus.
The slowdown in the rate of growth prompted a rise in unemployment to 3.1 percent in 1996 from 2.6 percent in 1995. It is forecast to settle back to 2.9 percent in 1997.

Inflation also rose to 3.0 percent in 1996 from 2.6 percent in 1995. It is expected to remain steady at 3.0 percent in 1997 based on the restrained rate of increase in labour costs, the gradual liberalisation of trade and a reduction in interest rates.

Tourism, the mainstay of the island's economy, is expected to exhibit a 3.0 percent increase in 1997 after an estimated decline by 5.5 in 1996. Tourism accounted for an estimated 20 percent of GDP in 1996.
The real average rate of growth of private consumption is forecast to grow 3.5 percent in 1997, from 3.0 percent in 1996.

The rate of increase of public consumption, including defence, is expected to fluctuate at around 4.5 percent, down from 10 percent in 1996 due mainly to the containment in the rate of increase of defence imports.
Excluding imports of defence equipment the rate of expansion of public consumption is expected to be contained to 3.5 percent in 1997, compared to 4 percent in 1996, the report said.
External demand will grow by 6.0 percent in 1997, from a growth rate of 5.5 percent in 1996, with a significant recovery in the export of goods and services.
The manufacturing sector is expected to expand by 1.0 percent in 1997 after a 2.0 percent decline in 1996, while construction is forecast to grow by 1.5 percent in 1997 from 1.0 percent in 1996.
Agriculture is not expected to show any signs of growth in 1997, after a 1.0 percent drop in production in real terms in 1996.
The island continues to suffer a severe drought resulting in the decline in crop production. Livestock production had slightly increased, it said.-- Nicosia newsroom 357 2 469625
